sections.h2: Which towns sit inside Banks County, and how did it begin?
sections.html:
Banks County lies in Georgia's northeast corner and Homer is its seat. The General Assembly passed the founding act on December 11, 1858, and the county took effect on February 1, 1859, cut from Franklin and Habersham counties (Wikipedia).

Wikipedia, using Census Bureau area data, gives the county 234 square miles, with 232 of them land. All of it falls within the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah River basin, and a slice of the Chattahoochee National Forest reaches in. Habersham, Stephens, Franklin, Madison, Jackson and Hall counties touch the border.

Cities listed are Baldwin, Commerce, Gillsville and Lula; towns are Alto, Homer and Maysville. Several of these straddle a line with Habersham, Jackson or Hall. Hollingsworth and Narrows are unincorporated. Because a mailing address can name a town that sits partly in a neighboring county, check the parcel record to learn which tax commissioner bills you.

Homer's Old Banks County Courthouse is on the National Register of Historic Places, and a newer courthouse went up beside it in 1983. Atlanta Dragway operates near Banks Crossing. Banks County School District, headquartered in Homer, runs four schools for roughly 2,788 students, and The Banks County News serves as the legal organ.

sections.h2: How fast is Banks County growing, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Growth has been brisk lately. The 2020 census counted 18,035 residents, and QuickFacts estimates 21,273 for mid-2025, up 17.6% from its adjusted 2020 base. For 2020-2024 the middle household income is $77,063 and the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $278,100.

A 32.7-minute commute is the second longest among the four counties in the QuickFacts comparison, behind Barrow. In the 2020 count, 95.6% of residents lived in rural areas, with 7,211 housing units and 7.8% of them vacant. That count also showed 6,652 households, with children under 18 in 33.9% of them, a median age of 40.6, and 77.8% of occupied units owned by their residents.

The long view is steeper than the recent one. Banks County had 6,497 people in 1960, 14,422 in 2000 and 18,395 in 2010, then slipped to 18,035 in 2020 before the newer estimate jumped. A county that quadrupled over six decades has plenty of houses of very different ages, from farmhouses to recent subdivisions, and buyers compare them closely.

sections.h2: Where do Banks County property tax questions go?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner bills and collects for the county, the state, the school board and community improvement districts. Property taxes are paid at Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547. The county's payment page says the Annex keeps weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

The phone for tax bills is 706-677-6204. For valuation, appeals, or news that a property was sold or a business closed after January 1, call the Board of Assessors at 706-677-6223. The commissioner honors a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated by midnight of the deadline; a postage-meter date does not count as proof.

  • Suite 7: property taxes in person
  • Tax commissioner phone: 706-677-6204
  • Board of Assessors phone: 706-677-6223

sections.h2: What does a Banks County assessment notice tell me?
sections.html:
Every owner of taxable real property gets an annual notice. It lists the fair market value fixed by the Board of Tax Assessors and the assessed value, which state law sets at 40%.

The assessors study sales in groups, by neighborhood, property type and use, and adjust whole groups when market evidence says values have drifted. A changed value shows on the notice. Disagreeing owners have 45 days from the notice date to appeal, on grounds of taxability, value or non-uniform assessment.

Bills usually arrive in September. If your parcel was under appeal then, the bill used a temporary value: the smaller of last year's value or 85% of this year's original notice value. It remained due on the printed date. After the appeal ends, the commissioner decides whether a supplemental bill or a credit follows.

sections.h2: How should I handle Banks County tax during a sale?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner states that it does not prorate tax between a buyer and a seller. Liability is settled at closing, usually with the purchaser assuming it, and your closing paperwork shows who pays. The tax attaches to the property, so whoever holds title should confirm it is paid.

A business that closed, or a property that sold, after January 1 still owes tax for the full year, and the Board of Assessors should be told. If a mortgage company pays your tax, the office would like you to forward them a copy of the bill.

  • A missing bill is not an excuse; copies are online or at the office
  • Partial payments are accepted until the bill is paid, by arrangement at 706-677-6204
  • Write the parcel ID on a check or money order

sections.h2: What if a Banks County appeal is still open on the due date?
sections.html:
Pay at least the appealed amount by the due date, the county's FAQ says, or a 1% penalty applies. Payment cannot be put off, and the assessors cannot extend the deadline. Interest of 1% per month, capped at $150, builds on the rest, and paying the full bill by the due date avoids it.

When you plan to sell during an appeal, tell your closing agent. The final figure may change, a supplemental bill or credit may follow, and you should agree in writing who keeps any refund.

sections.h2: How do Banks County exemptions get approved?
sections.html:
Nothing here is automatic; each exemption needs its own application. The name on the deed must match the applicant, who must own, occupy and claim the home as a legal residence on January 1. The county asks for proof of residency and citizenship or legal authorization, plus current registration or receipts for vehicles owned in Banks County.

A married couple counts as one applicant and gets one exemption. Once granted it renews, and a refinance does not require filing again. Changes of name or ownership through marriage, death or divorce mean reapplying with a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. Faxed or emailed applications are rejected; an original must arrive, or carry a non-metered postmark, by the April 1 deadline for a first-year claim.

Forms and instructions are on the county's Tax Assessors page. Look there for current local amounts before you list.

sections.h2: What is the first move for a Banks County seller with tax due?
sections.html:
Call 706-677-6204 and ask what is owed on the parcel for the current and any earlier years. If part of the balance is under appeal, say so in the same call, since the temporary-value bill rules apply. Then give your closing agent the amount and the Suite 7 address, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer.

If an exemption is on the property and you are moving, tell the tax commissioner when you no longer qualify. The county's FAQ says the office must be notified if the applicant no longer meets the requirements, and a buyer who wants a homestead exemption must apply on their own after closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Banks County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Go to Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex at 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547, open weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. Mailing a payment or using the online payment link also works.

faqs.q: Will the Banks County tax commissioner divide the bill between me and the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The office says it stays out of the buyer and seller proration. Your closing documents decide who pays.

faqs.q: Can I submit a faxed homestead form in Banks County?
faqs.a: No. The county's FAQ says an original must be received or postmarked by the deadline, and faxed or emailed copies are not accepted.

faqs.q: May I pay a Banks County bill in pieces?
faqs.a: Yes. Partial payments are accepted until the bill is satisfied, and the county asks you to call 706-677-6204 to set it up. Interest keeps accruing on what remains.

faqs.q: What if no bill ever came?
faqs.a: The responsibility to pay by the due date still stands. A copy is on the county website or available from the tax commissioner.
